chapter.li: Verse27 And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi. And by the way, he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am? VerseEnd Verse28 And they answered, John the Baptist; but some say Elijah, and others, one of the prophets. VerseEnd Verse29 And he said unto them, But whom do you say that I am? And Peter answered and said unto him, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. VerseEnd Verse30 And he charged them that they should tell no man of him. VerseEnd

Verse31 And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and the chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again. VerseEnd Verse32 And he spoke that saying openly. And Peter took him and began to rebuke him. VerseEnd Verse33 But when he had turned about and looked upon his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get behind me, Satan, for you savor not the things that are of God, but the things that are of men. VerseEnd

Verse34 And when he had called the people, with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whoever will come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me; VerseEnd Verse35 for whoever will save his life shall lose it, or whoever will save his life shall be willing to lay it down for my sake. And if he is not willing to lay it down for my sake, he shall lose it. But whoever shall be willing to lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it. VerseEnd Verse36 For what shall it profit a man if he shall gain the whole world and lose his own soul? VerseEnd Verse37 Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul? Therefore, deny yourselves of these, and be not ashamed of me. VerseEnd

Verse38 Whoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, of him also shall the Son of Man be ashamed when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy VerseEnd LEChapter9 Verse1 angels. And they shall not have part in that resurrection when he comes. For truly I say unto you that he shall come, and he that lays down his life for my sake and the gospel’s shall come with him, and shall be clothed with his glory in the cloud, on the right hand of the Son of Man. And he said unto them again, Truly I say unto you that there are some of them that stand here who shall not taste of death until they have seen the kingdom of God come with power. VerseEnd

Verse2 And after six days, Jesus took Peter, and James, and John, who asked him many questions concerning his saying. And Jesus leads them up into a high mountain, apart by themselves, and he was transfigured before them. VerseEnd Verse3 And his raiment became shining, exceedingly white as snow, so white as no fuller on earth could white them. VerseEnd Verse4 And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses, or in other words, John the Baptist and Moses; and they were talking with Jesus. VerseEnd Verse5 And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here, and let us make three tabernacles: one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elias; VerseEnd Verse6 for he knew not what to say, for they were sorely afraid. VerseEnd Verse7 And there was a cloud that overshadowed them. And a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my Beloved Son; hear him. VerseEnd

Verse8 And suddenly, when they had looked round about with great astonishment, they saw no man anymore, save Jesus only with themselves. VerseEnd Verse9 And immediately they departed. And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead. VerseEnd Verse10 And they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean. VerseEnd

Verse11 And they asked him, saying, Why do the scribes say that Elias must first come? VerseEnd Verse12 And he answered and told them, saying, Elias truly comes first, and prepares all things, and teaches you of the prophets, how it is written of the Son of Man that he must suffer many things and be set at naught. VerseEnd Verse13 Again I say unto you that Elias has indeed come, but they have done unto him whatever they desired, and even as it is written of him. And he bore record of me and they received him not. Truly this was Elias. VerseEnd

Verse14 And when he came to the disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them. VerseEnd Verse15 And immediately all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to him, saluted him. VerseEnd Verse16 And Jesus asked the scribes, What did you question with them? VerseEnd Verse17 And one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought unto you my son, who has a dumb spirit VerseEnd Verse18 that is a devil. And when he seizes him, he throws him down; and he foams, and gnashes with his teeth, and wastes away. And I spoke to your disciples, that they might cast him out, and they could not. VerseEnd Verse19 Jesus spoke unto him and said, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you? Bring him unto me. VerseEnd

Verse20 And they brought him unto Jesus, and when the man saw him, immediately he was convulsed by the spirit, and he fell on the ground and wallowed, foaming. VerseEnd Verse21 And Jesus asked his father, How long a time is it since this came unto him? And his father said, When a child; VerseEnd Verse22 and ofttimes it has cast him into the fire and into the waters, to destroy him. But if you can, I ask you to have compassion on us and help us. VerseEnd Verse23 Jesus said unto him, If you will believe all things I shall say unto you, this is possible to him that believes. VerseEnd Verse24 And immediately the father of the child cried out and said with tears, Lord, I believe! Help my unbelief. VerseEnd

Verse25 When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, saying unto him, I charge you to come out of him and enter no more into him. VerseEnd Verse26 Now the dumb and deaf spirit cried and convulsed him severely, and came out of him. And he was as one dead, insomuch that many said, He is dead. VerseEnd Verse27 But Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him up, and he arose. VerseEnd

Verse28 When Jesus had come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, Why could we not cast him out? VerseEnd Verse29 And he said unto them, This kind can come forth by nothing but by prayer and fasting. VerseEnd

Verse30 And they departed from there and passed through Galilee privately, for he desired not that any man should know it. VerseEnd Verse31 And he taught his disciples and said unto them, The Son of Man is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him. And after he is killed, he shall rise the third day. VerseEnd Verse32 But they understood not that saying, and were afraid to ask him. VerseEnd

Verse33 And he came to Capernaum. And being in the house, he asked them, Why was it that you disputed among yourselves by the way? VerseEnd Verse34 But they held their peace, being afraid, for by the way they had disputed among themselves who was the greatest among them. VerseEnd Verse35 Now Jesus sat down and called the twelve and said unto them, If any man desire to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all. VerseEnd Verse36 And he took a child and sat in the middle of them. And when he had taken the child in his arms, he said unto them, VerseEnd Verse37 Whoever shall humble himself like one of these children, and receives me, you shall receive in my name. And whoever shall receive me, receives not me only, but him that sent me, even the Father. VerseEnd

Verse38 And John spoke unto him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils in your name, and he followed not us, and we forbade him because he follows not us. VerseEnd Verse39 But Jesus said, Forbid him not, for there is no man who shall do a miracle in my name that can speak evil of me; VerseEnd Verse40 for he that is not against us is on our part. VerseEnd

Verse41 And whoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because you belong to Christ, truly I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward. VerseEnd Verse42 And whoever shall offend one of these little ones that believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone were hung about his neck, and he were cast into the sea. VerseEnd

Verse43 Therefore, if your hand offend you, cut it off. Or if your brother offend you, and confess not and forsake not, he shall be cut off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed than having two hands to go into hell. For it is better for you to enter into life without your brother than for you and your brother to be cast into hell — into the fire that never shall be quenched, VerseEnd Verse44 where their worm dies not and the fire is not quenched. VerseEnd

Verse45 And again, if your foot offend you, cut it off. For he that is your standard by whom you walk, if he become a transgressor, he shall be cut off. It is better for you to enter lame into life than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched. VerseEnd Verse46 Therefore, let every man stand or fall by himself, and not for another, or not trusting another.

Seek unto my Father and it shall be done in that very moment what you shall ask, if you ask in faith, believing that you shall receive. VerseEnd Verse47 And if your eye which sees for you — him who is appointed to watch over you to show you light — becomes a transgressor and offends you, pluck him out. It is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than having two eyes to be cast into hellfire; for it is better that you should be saved than to be cast into hell with your brother, VerseEnd Verse48 where their worm dies not and where the fire is not quenched. VerseEnd

Verse49 For everyone shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt VerseEnd — Verse50 but the salt must be good; for if the salt has lost its saltiness, with what will you season it (the sacrifice)? Therefore, it must be that you have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another. VerseEnd

LEChapter10 Verse1 And he arose from there, and comes into the borders of Judea by the farther side of Jordan. And the people gathered unto him again, and as he was accustomed to teach, he also taught them again. VerseEnd Verse2 And the Pharisees came to him and asked him, Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife? This they said, thinking to test him. VerseEnd Verse3 And he answered and said unto them, What did Moses command you? VerseEnd Verse4 And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement and to divorce her. VerseEnd Verse5 Jesus answered and said unto them, For the hardness of your hearts he wrote you this precept, VerseEnd Verse6 but from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female. VerseEnd Verse7 For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother and cleave to his wife, VerseEnd Verse8 and they two shall be one flesh. So then they are no more two, but one flesh. VerseEnd Verse9 What therefore God has joined together, let not man put asunder. VerseEnd

Verse10 And in the house, his disciples asked him again of the same matter. VerseEnd Verse11 And he said unto them, Whoever shall divorce his wife and marry another commits adultery against her. VerseEnd Verse12 And if a woman shall divorce her husband and be married to another, she commits adultery. VerseEnd

Verse13 And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them, and the disciples rebuked those that brought them. VerseEnd Verse14 But when Jesus saw and heard them, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me and forbid them not, for of such is the kingdom of God. VerseEnd Verse15 Truly I say unto you, whoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein. VerseEnd Verse16 And he took them up in his arms, and put his hands upon them and blessed them. VerseEnd

Verse17 And when he had gone forth into the way, there came one running, and kneeled to him and asked him, Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life? VerseEnd Verse18 And Jesus said unto him, Why do you call me good? None is good but one — that is, God. VerseEnd Verse19 You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery; do not kill; do not steal; do not bear false witness; defraud not; honor your father and mother. VerseEnd Verse20 And the man answered and said unto him, Master, all these have I observed from my youth. VerseEnd Verse21 Then Jesus, beholding him, loved him and said unto him, One thing you lack: go your way, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in Heaven; and come take up the cross and follow me. VerseEnd Verse22 And the man was sad at that saying and went away grieved, for he had great possessions. VerseEnd

Verse23 And Jesus looked round about and said unto his disciples, How difficultly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of my Father. And the disciples were astonished at his words. VerseEnd Verse24 But Jesus spoke again and said unto them, Children, how hard is it for them who trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God? VerseEnd Verse25 It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. VerseEnd Verse26 And they were astonished out of measure, saying among themselves, Who then can be saved? VerseEnd Verse27 And Jesus, looking upon them, said, With men that trust in riches, it is impossible; but not impossible with men who trust in God and leave all for my sake. For with such, all these things are possible. VerseEnd

Verse28 Then Peter began to say unto him, Behold, we have left all and have followed you. VerseEnd Verse29 And Jesus answered and said, Truly I say unto you, there is no man that has left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake and the gospel’s, but VerseEnd Verse30 he shall receive a hundredfold now in this time — houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions — and in the world to come, eternal life. VerseEnd Verse31 But there are many who make themselves first that shall be last, and the last, first. This he said rebuking Peter. VerseEnd Verse32 And they were in the way going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus went before, and they were amazed.

And as they followed, they were afraid. And he took again the twelve and began to tell them what things should happen unto him. VerseEnd Verse33 And Jesus said, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be delivered unto the chief priests and unto the scribes. And they shall condemn him to death and shall deliver him to the Gentiles. VerseEnd Verse34 And they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit upon him, and shall kill him; and the third day, he shall rise again. VerseEnd

Verse35 And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came unto him, saying, Master, we wish that you should do for us whatever we shall desire. VerseEnd Verse36 And he said unto them, What do you desire that I should do unto VerseEnd Verse37 you? They said unto him, Grant unto us that we may sit one on your right hand and the other on your left hand in your glory. VerseEnd Verse38 But Jesus said unto them, you know not what you ask. Can you drink of the cup that I drink of? And be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? VerseEnd Verse39 And they said unto him, We can. And Jesus said unto them, You shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with. VerseEnd Verse40 But to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give, but they shall receive it for whom it is prepared. VerseEnd

Verse41 And when the ten heard, they began to be much displeased with James and John. VerseEnd Verse42 But Jesus called them and said unto them, You know that they who are appointed to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and their great ones exercise authority upon them. VerseEnd Verse43 But it shall not be so among you. But whoever will be great among you shall be your minister, VerseEnd Verse44 and whoever of you will be the chiefest shall be servant of all. VerseEnd Verse45 For even the Son of Man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many. VerseEnd

Verse46 And they came to Jericho. And as he went out of Jericho, with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimaeus (the son of Timaeus) sat by the highway side, begging. VerseEnd Verse47 And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out and say, Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me! VerseEnd Verse48 And many charged him that he should hold his peace, but he cried the more exceedingly, saying, Son of David, have mercy on me! VerseEnd Verse49 And Jesus stood still and commanded him to be called. And they called the blind man, saying unto him, Be of good comfort; arise, he calls you. VerseEnd Verse50 And he, casting away his garment, arose and came to Jesus. VerseEnd Verse51 And Jesus said unto him, What do you desire that I should do unto you? And the blind man said unto him, Lord, that I might receive my sight. VerseEnd Verse52 And Jesus said unto him, Go your way, your faith has made you whole. And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus in the way. VerseEnd

LEChapter11 Verse1 And when they came near to Jerusalem, unto Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent forth two of his disciples VerseEnd Verse2 and said unto them, Go your way into the village ahead of you; and as soon as you have entered into it, you shall find a colt tied, on which no man ever sat. Untie him and bring him to me. VerseEnd Verse3 And if any man say unto you, Why are you doing this? — say that the Lord has need of him, and immediately he will send him here. VerseEnd

Verse4 And they went their way and found the colt tied by the door outside, in a place where two ways met. And they untied him. VerseEnd Verse5 And certain of them who stood by said unto the disciples, Why are you untying the colt? VerseEnd Verse6 And they said unto them even as Jesus had commanded, and they let them go. VerseEnd Verse7 And they brought the colt to Jesus and cast their garments on it, and Jesus sat upon it. VerseEnd Verse8 And many spread their garments in the way, and others cut down branches off of the trees and strewed them in the way. VerseEnd

Verse9 And they that went before him and they that followed after cried, saying, Hosanna! Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord, VerseEnd Verse10 that brings the kingdom of our father David! Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest! VerseEnd Verse11 And Jesus entered into Jerusalem and into the temple. And when he had looked round about upon all things and blessed the disciples, the hour had come. And he went out unto Bethany with the twelve. VerseEnd

Verse12 And on the next day, when they came from Bethany, he was hungry. VerseEnd Verse13 And seeing a fig tree afar off, having leaves, he came to it with his disciples. And as they supposed, he came to it to see if he might find anything thereon. And when he came to it, there was nothing but leaves, for as yet the figs were not ripe. VerseEnd Verse14 And Jesus spoke and said unto it, No man eat fruit of you hereafter, for ever. And his disciples heard him. VerseEnd

Verse15 And they came to Jerusalem. And Jesus went into the temple and began to cast out them who sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers and the seats of them who sold doves, VerseEnd Verse16 and would not suffer that any man should carry a vessel through the temple. VerseEnd Verse17 And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written: My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? But you have made it a den of thieves. VerseEnd Verse18 And the scribes and chief priests heard him, and sought how they might destroy him; for they feared him, because all the people were astonished at his teachings. VerseEnd Verse19 And when evening had come, he went out of the city. VerseEnd

Verse20 And in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots. VerseEnd Verse21 And Peter, calling to remembrance, said unto him, Master, behold, the fig tree which you cursed is withered away. VerseEnd Verse22 And Jesus spoke and said unto him, Have faith in God. VerseEnd Verse23 For truly I say unto you that whoever shall say unto this mountain: Be removed, and be cast into the sea — and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he says shall come to pass — he shall have whatever he says fulfilled. VerseEnd Verse24 Therefore, I say unto you, whatever things you desire when you pray, believe that you receive, and you shall have whatever you ask. VerseEnd Verse25 And when you stand praying, forgive if you have anything against any, that your Father also who is in Heaven may forgive you your trespasses. VerseEnd Verse26 But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in Heaven forgive your trespasses. VerseEnd

Verse27 And they came again to Jerusalem. And as he was walking in the temple, there came to him the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders, VerseEnd Verse28 and said unto him, By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority to do these things? VerseEnd Verse29 And Jesus answered and said unto them, I will also ask of you one question. Answer me, and then I will tell you by what authority I do these things. VerseEnd Verse30 Was the baptism of John from Heaven or of men? Answer me. VerseEnd Verse31 And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From Heaven, he will say, Why then did you not believe him? VerseEnd Verse32 But if we shall say, Of men, we shall offend the people. Therefore, they feared the people, for all people believed John, that he was a prophet indeed. VerseEnd Verse33 And they answered and said unto Jesus, We cannot tell. And Jesus, answering, said unto them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things. VerseEnd

LEChapter12 Verse1 And Jesus began to speak unto them by parables, saying, A man planted a vineyard, and set a hedge about it, and dug the wine vat, and built a tower, and leased it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country. VerseEnd Verse2 And at the season, he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard. VerseEnd Verse3 And they caught the servant, and beat him, and sent him away empty. VerseEnd Verse4 And again he sent unto them another servant, and at him they cast stones and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled. VerseEnd Verse5 And again he sent another, and him they killed, and many others — beating some and killing some. VerseEnd

Verse6 Having yet therefore one son, his well-beloved, he sent him also last unto them, saying, They will reverence my son. VerseEnd Verse7 But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him and the inheritance shall be ours. VerseEnd Verse8 And they took him and cast him out of the vineyard and killed him. VerseEnd Verse9 What shall therefore the Lord of the vineyard do? Behold, he will come and destroy the husbandmen and will give the vineyard unto others. VerseEnd Verse10 Again, have you not read this scripture: The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; VerseEnd Verse11 this was the Lord’s doing and it is marvelous in our eyes? VerseEnd

Verse12 And now they were angry when they heard these words, and they sought to lay hold on him, but feared the people, for they knew that he had spoken the parable against them. And they left him and went their way. VerseEnd

Verse13 And they sent unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians to catch him in words. VerseEnd Verse14 And when they had come, they said unto him, Master, we know that you are true and care for no man; for you regard not the person of men, but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar or not? VerseEnd Verse15 Shall we give or shall we not give?

But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said unto them, Why do you test me? Bring me a penny, that I may see it. VerseEnd Verse16 And they brought the penny. And he said unto them, Whose image and superscription is this? And they said unto him, Caesar’s. VerseEnd Verse17 And Jesus, answering, said unto them, Render to Caesar the things which are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s. And they marveled at it. VerseEnd

Verse18 Then came unto him the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection. And they asked him, saying, VerseEnd Verse19 Master, Moses wrote unto us in his law: If a man’s brother die and leave a wife, and leave no children, that his brother should take his wife and raise up seed unto his brother. VerseEnd Verse20 Now there were seven brethren. The first took a wife, and dying, left no seed. VerseEnd Verse21 And the second took her, and died, neither left he any seed; and the third likewise. VerseEnd Verse22 And the seven had her and left no seed. Last of all the woman died also. VerseEnd Verse23 In the resurrection, therefore, when they shall rise, whose wife shall she be of them? For the seven had her to wife. VerseEnd

Verse24 And Jesus, answering, said unto them, You do err therefore because you know not and understand not the scriptures, neither the power of God. VerseEnd Verse25 For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God who are in Heaven. VerseEnd Verse26 And as touching the dead, that they rise, have you not read in the book of Moses how in the bush God spoke unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? VerseEnd Verse27 He is not therefore the God of the dead, but the God of the living, for he raises them up out of their graves. You therefore do greatly err. VerseEnd

Verse28 And one of the scribes came, and having heard them reasoning together, and perceiving that he had answered them well, asked him, Which is the first commandment of all? VerseEnd Verse29 And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is: Listen, and hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord. VerseEnd Verse30 And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength. This is the first commandment. VerseEnd Verse31 And the second is like this: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these. VerseEnd

Verse32 And the scribe said unto him, Well, Master, you have said the truth; for there is one God, and there is none other but him. VerseEnd Verse33 And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices. VerseEnd Verse34 And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said unto him, You are not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that dare ask him, saying, Who are you? VerseEnd

Verse35 And Jesus spoke and said, while he taught in the temple, How do the scribes say that Christ is the son of David? VerseEnd Verse36 For David himself said by the holy ghost: The Lord said unto my Lord, You sit on my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool. VerseEnd Verse37 David therefore himself called him Lord, and from where is he his son? And the common people heard him gladly, VerseEnd Verse38 but the high priest and the elders were offended at him.

And he said unto them in his teachings, Beware of the scribes who love to go in long clothing and have salutations in the marketplaces, VerseEnd Verse39 and the chief seats in the synagogues, and the uppermost rooms at feasts; VerseEnd Verse40 who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These shall receive greater damnation. VerseEnd

Verse41 And after this, Jesus sat opposite the treasury and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury; and many that were rich cast in much. VerseEnd Verse42 And there came a certain poor widow, and she cast in two mites, which make a farthing. VerseEnd Verse43 And Jesus called his disciples and said unto them, Truly I say unto you that this poor widow has cast more in than all they who have cast into the treasury; VerseEnd Verse44 for all the rich did cast in of their abundance, but she — notwithstanding her lack — did cast in all that she had; yea, even all her possessions. VerseEnd
